catalog_quote: Stress refers to the emphasis given to a particular syllable. The loudness of a syllable characterizes it. The symbol [‘] is used in this study as a symbol for stress. This symbol is placed before the stressed syllable. As shown in the examples below, word or lexical stress in Higaonon is phonemic. When the placement of the stress changes, the meaning of the word also changes. [‘sa.la] ‘punishment’ / [sa.’la] ‘sin’ / [‘su.ləd] ‘sibling’ / [su.’ləd] ‘inside’. Meanwhile, stress is placed on the ultimate or penultimate syllable of Higaonon words. Stress on the ultimate syllable: [tun.’lo] ‘finger’, [tə.’ŋəl] ‘nape’, [pi.’lək] ‘eyelash’, [ku.’diŋ] ‘cat’. Stress on the penultimate syllable: [‘ba.he] ‘woman’, [‘ka.ʔən] ‘eat’, [‘kag.pa] ‘chest’, [‘su.lo] ‘fingernail’. ... [Conclusion, p. 64:] Word stress in this language is phonemic.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is contrastive (phonemic): it falls on either the final or the penultimate syllable of the word and its position is not predictable from the segmental shape, as shown by minimal pairs distinguished by stress alone (sala 'punishment' vs sala 'sin'; suled 'sibling' vs suled 'inside'). The source gives no default position, no weight or morphological conditioning, and no statement about which position is more common; the window is the last two syllables.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned anywhere in the article.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the description is example-based (four ultimate, four penultimate, two minimal pairs) and states only that stress is placed on the ultimate or penultimate syllable.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: the section is titled 'Word Stress', speaks of 'word or lexical stress' and 'Higaonon words', and the data are elicited citation-form words and sentences collected from tribal leaders of the Opol (Misamis Oriental) variety; nothing on phrase-level or affixed-form stress.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement describes the Higaonon variety of Opol, Misamis Oriental (data from Opol tribal leaders), explicitly labelled Higaonon [ISO 639-3 mba] = Glottolog higa1237. Abingosa et al. note (citing KWF 2023) that vowel phonemes differ between Bukidnon/Claveria varieties and other Higaonon communities, so the ult/penult contrast is attested for Opol only. Closely related Binukid (Talaandig-Binukid, binu1244, 77-81% intelligibility) is already in the catalog from Post & Gardner 1992 with the same phonemic-stress pattern (sala/sala minimal pair, usually penult); Glottolog keeps the two as separate languoids under 'Bukidnon'.
